page: Microsoft Azure E8as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Easv7 family, utilizing x86_64 AMD processors under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 8 dedicated virtual processor cores matched with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-to-core allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware virtualization flags, extended vector extensions, and hardware security attributes report as unexposed in the baseline specification profile.

The instance does not incorporate bundled local storage, operating without direct physical disk attachments and relying instead on external block devices such as Premium Storage. Graphical processing capabilities are not included, with a GPU count of zero. Network provisioning includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard Azure virtual network configurations for public ingress and egress connectivity.

With its high memory density per compute unit, the architecture offers resource efficiency for environments where RAM capacity limits scalability prior to CPU saturation. This allocation profile suits memory-intensive enterprise workloads including relational databases, in-memory key-value caches, intermediate data transform jobs, and enterprise business applications requiring sizable volatile memory structures alongside remote persistent storage.
